note: Only paragraph (a) differs: A covers any person not excluded by Dodd-Frank section 1029, while B covers state member banks, certain foreign bank offices and Edge/agreement corporations; the medical-information rule is otherwise identical.
The two texts are identical.

A has paragraph (h), the 2013 partial exemption for certain subordinate-lien housing-assistance loans, plus a note on a 2024 paragraph (i), while B stops at (g) with a 2011 citation; the other differences are wording.

The visible differences are cross-reference numbering (N.60/N.40 against N.5a/N.5b), reserved footnote markers and a 'Timing requirements' heading; the rule text matches as far as the truncated texts go.
The only difference is where a semicolon sits relative to a closing quotation mark.

A adds joint-relationship rules for credit unions and for FTC-jurisdiction entities, and a reply-form address requirement for the latter, because it covers those institutions; B covers only the banks, whose rule matches A's paragraph (d).

A keeps the old two-part ATM fee notice (a sign on the machine plus a screen or paper notice) and a 2004 temporary exemption, citing 2006, while B has the 2013 amendment that requires only the screen or paper notice.
Subpart E covers state member banks and related foreign bank and Edge entities in A, and any furnisher not excluded by Dodd-Frank section 1029 in B.

A has the 2013 HOEPA amendments (high-cost mortgages including open-end account opening, open-end APR tolerances, and the new paragraph (h) on corrections and unintentional violations), while B keeps the 2007 closed-end-only version.
A names 'appendix A' and has a 2009 source citation, B says 'the appendix'; the rule is the same.

A extends the purpose and coverage to remittance transfer services and to persons other than financial institutions (the issuing agency's remittance-transfer jurisdiction), while B covers electronic fund transfers by financial institutions only; OMB numbers and agency naming also differ.

B lacks the later amendments in A: the first-year fee cap no longer counts fees before account opening, the safe-harbor amounts have been raised ($32/$43), and there is an $8 late-fee safe harbor with a smaller-card-issuer exception; B keeps the 2010 $25/$35 safe harbors.

B adds the record-retention provisions for subpart B (small business lending data) and for information collected under § N.5(a)(4), from the 2017 and 2023 amendments, which A, last amended in 2011, lacks.

The redisclosure limit itself is identical; A applies it to member banks, holding companies and other entities under one agency's jurisdiction, while B applies it to any person not excluded by Dodd-Frank section 1029.

Apart from abbreviating the FCRA, the only change is that A defines identity theft by cross-reference to 16 CFR 603.2(a) and B omits that definition here; the furnisher accuracy and integrity definitions are the same.

B keeps the 2010 rule that ability to pay must rest on the consumer's independent income or assets, and lacks A's 2013 amendment allowing income and assets to which the consumer has a reasonable expectation of access, along with the matching credit-line-increase provision for young consumers in (b)(2)(i).
B (2010) lacks the 2021/2023 LIBOR-transition amendments that A has: the replacement-index termination of the review obligation in (f)(3) and the LIBOR-transition exception in (h)(3).

B has the 2013 amendment that A lacks, which sends preemption of the RESPA sections 4 and 5 integrated-disclosure requirements (§§ N.19(e)-(f), N.37, N.38) through this section; B also updates the card-disclosure cross-reference to § N.60.
The two texts are identical.

B is pre-Dodd-Frank: it lists the Office of Thrift Supervision, has no consumer-financial-protection agency, and sets a two-year limitations period, whereas A has the post-2010 five-year period and the CFPB-era enforcement assignments.

The two texts are different provisions sharing a section number (A is the dwelling-secured ability-to-repay/qualified-mortgage rule, B is the higher-priced mortgage loan appraisal rule), so a like-for-like comparison is not possible.

A's paragraph (i) carries the prepaid-account/hybrid prepaid-credit card amendments and cites 12 CFR 1005.11 and 1005.18(e), while B keeps the 2010 text citing 12 CFR 205.11 with no prepaid provisions.
B is the 2010 text lacking the later RESPA/TILA integrated-disclosure, FIRREA, high-cost mortgage and section 1029 coverage amendments that A has taken, along with older cross-references (N.5a/N.5b).
Only capitalization of 'State', 'part' versus 'regulation', and a citation line differ; the state-exemption rule is the same.

B is the 2001/2008 HOEPA version keyed to loans subject to § N.32 with a seven-year repayment-ability presumption, lacking the 2013 high-cost mortgage amendments (open-end coverage, pre-loan counseling, ATR cross-reference to § N.43) that A has.
B lacks paragraph (a)(4) permitting collection of demographic information for HMDA-excluded loans (2017) and small-business applications (2023), which A has taken.

B includes an example making an auto dealer that is the original creditor responsible for the risk-based pricing notice, which A omits, consistent with A's agency lacking authority over auto dealers; the rule is otherwise identical.

B is the 2009/2010 text citing Regulation Z part 226 and lacking the 2016 prepaid-account and hybrid prepaid-credit card provisions that A has (A also corrects the civil liability section from 915 to 916).

A applies to insured nonmember banks supervised by its agency, while B applies to all GLB Act financial institutions under its agency's rulemaking authority, excluding auto dealers, SEC/CFTC-regulated entities and others, and adds a FERPA compliance provision.
B excludes persons covered by Dodd-Frank section 1029 (auto dealers) and names its own agency and OMB number, while A covers all creditors under the older agency text; the purpose is the same.

A keeps the expired 1993-1994 disaster-area rescission waivers, the old footnote structure and a material-disclosures cross-reference to N.35(b)(2), and lacks the 2013-era N.43(g) reference and total-of-payments tolerances that B has; A appears older.

A is the 2008/2011 higher-priced mortgage loan rule (repayment ability, prepayment penalties, 365-day escrow cancellation), while B has the later rewrite with small-creditor and rural/underserved escrow exemptions, five-year escrow cancellation and appraisal rules; A appears older.
Only cross-reference wording differs ("of this part", added section symbols); the rule is identical.

B keeps the 1987 variable-rate adjustment notice (25-120 days, footnote 45c), while A has the 2013 ARM rate-adjustment disclosure rules with coverage, exemptions, 60-120 day timing and tabular format; B appears older.

B (amended through 2010) lacks the 2011-2012 coverage changes in A (the Dodd-Frank section 1029 exclusion and remittance transfer providers under subpart B) and still carries the expired 2007/2009 transitional notice provisions; B appears older.
Differences are quotation marks, "of this section" cross-references, "effective" vs "mandatory compliance" date wording and a statutory section number; the gift card rules are the same.

A (amended through 2010) lacks the 2013 changes in B that exclude mortgages subject to N.19(e) and (f), broaden the prepayment disclosure to any charge for paying all or part early, and move footnotes into the text; A appears older.

Coverage differs (A covers any person except those excluded by Dodd-Frank section 1029, B covers state member banks, foreign bank branches and similar institutions) and B says "depository" where A says "financial" institution; the affiliate-marketing definitions are otherwise the same.
B is the 2006 payroll card account rule, while A is the later prepaid accounts rule with pre-acquisition short/long form disclosures and 12/24-month histories; B appears older.
Differences are punctuation, capitalization, naming the AGENCY among law enforcement agencies and a cross-reference to N.7(f) vs N.7(h); the exceptions are the same.

B has the 2013 rule requiring creditors to provide copies of all appraisals and written valuations for first-lien dwelling loans, with timing, notice and waiver rules; A keeps the older rule of providing appraisal reports routinely or on written request, with a credit-union carve-out.
B adds the (b)(7) index-replacement and margin-change exception (including the LIBOR transition) that A lacks, and updates a cross-reference from N.5b to N.40; A seems older.
B has the integrated mortgage disclosure (N.19(e), (f), (g)) carve-outs and the N.20(d) separate-document requirement, which A lacks; A seems older.
The texts are identical.
The only differences are 'act/regulation' versus 'Act/part', a reserved footnote marker and the source citation; the rule is the same.
The only differences are a parenthesis and a missing source citation; the rule is the same.
B has the 2017 amendment that allows disaggregated ethnicity and race categories from appendix B to part 1003 and makes collection from co-applicants optional; A lacks it and seems older.

In A the Federal Trade Commission decides whether state law gives greater protection, after consulting AGENCY; in B AGENCY decides, after consulting the agency with GLB Act section 505(a) jurisdiction. So the deciding agency differs, but the preemption rule is the same.

A has the prepaid-account amendments (pre-acquisition disclosures, an electronic history covering 12 months, a written history covering 24 months, and modified liability and error-resolution rules); B keeps the 1997 version with a 60-day written history, so B seems older.
The only differences are 'Web site' versus 'Internet Web site', 'email' versus 'e-mail', and punctuation; the rule is the same.
